# §E — Rooms, threads, sessions and fork routing
**CHD-3.5 · SPEC V3.5 · specified; native binding remains OPEN G-04.**
> **REVISION NOTICE — supersedes CHD-3.4.** The former §E is replaced in full. Guessed native create/fork bodies and the competing chd-key-v1 recipe are retired. NEW and REUSE both target committed identity. D-039 governs replacement.

## E.1 Rooms and membership
A room is a permissioned work space with kind objective, task or space. Parent linkage represents work structure. Assignees, reviewers, observers and recipients require explicit grant-backed membership. Tags select scope but confer no permission. The controller expands post recipients into immutable `to_snapshot`; current membership controls subsequent reads and posts. A caller cannot forge sender, role or Crier authority. Unknown and unreadable targets return identical `404 not_found`, message `Target not found`, detail `{}`.
Only the controller allocates sequence. Message keys use `/chd/room/<room>/m<seq:012d>`. The record vocabulary is `msg`, `question`, `status`, `directive`, `task`, `report`, `incident`; ordinary post, typed report and service incident paths enforce different allowed subsets.

## E.2 Thread lineage and reading
A root has `reply_to:null,thread_root:null`. Replies name an existing lower sequence in the same room; the controller resolves stable root through ancestry. It rejects future-parent, cross-room and cyclic links. Thread reads include the root itself. Iterative bounded traversal avoids stack exhaustion. `since` is exclusive; results ascend by sequence after authorization/thread filtering. `next_since` is last returned sequence or original cursor if empty. `has_more` reflects remaining matching rows in the same authoritative snapshot. Gaps are permanent and legal. Reading has no shared ACK or cursor side effect.
A report joins send, attempt, bond generation, native identity and thread. A mismatch is rejected/audited and cannot wake unrelated work. A retired generation remains addressable for history; delayed replies never move to a newer generation simply because the agent name matches. CHD never synthesizes a native transcript from room history.

## E.3 Bonds and capacity
TABLE 5.1-1 — Identity boundaries
| Identity | Owned meaning | |---|---| | agent/room/subthread_root/work_uid/generation | One work branch; null members compare explicitly | | bond_id | Stable join to non-default profile and committed native session | | allocation ID | Immutable provisioning operation, retained after success | | send_id | Logical obligation spanning attempts | | attempt_id | Immutable target episode; exact retry retains identity | | run/reservation | Execution correlation and authoritative capacity ownership | | policy_rev | Session-bound effective snapshot, not archive source revision |
One agent can hold multiple bonds in a room. Root 42/work T-101 selects bond A/session A; root 57/work T-205 selects bond B/session B. Replies remain separate. Capacity counts held attempt/run reservations in §J's dimensions, not bond existence. A report, wait, timeout, cancelled send or missing process cannot release a slot.

## E.4 Allocate, commit identity, deliver The allocation ledger is retained unchanged. A separate delivery attempt targets the committed native session. NEW is a context label, not permission for a headerless first turn.

### E.4.1 Delivery sequence
The following sequence is the controller's numbered delivery procedure:
1. Authenticate, authorize and select the named profile. 2. Commit allocation intent, immutable request bytes, lineage and allocation ID. 3. A version-bound adapter performs create/fork/import. G-04/G-07 must bind transport, version, errors and unknown-outcome lookup before activation. 4. Reconcile returned native identity/lineage; commit allocation result and bond. 5. Commit delivery attempt, full target identity, canonical bytes/digest, scoped key and reservation. 6. Both NEW and REUSE explicitly target the committed `X-Hermes-Session-Id` and selected memory-scope key. 7. A lost allocation response is reconciled by retained allocation identity; no speculative second child is allowed. Unknown execution retains capacity.
No exact native create/fork/import HTTP body is selected here. Historical `/api/sessions` examples do not establish a version-bound adapter. Capability discovery is not proof of response-loss reconciliation or import compatibility.

## E.5 Canonical gateway identity
The selected target has exactly these eight members:
```json { "gateway_ref": "gw-main", "agent_id": "mgr-a", "profile_ref": "profile-a", "native_session_id": "session-a", "session_allocation_id": null, "room_id": "room-a", "thread_root": null, "work_uid": null } ```
Exactly one of native session/allocation ID is nonempty and the other null. Thread is null or a positive exact integer; work UID is null or nonempty; other members are nonempty strings. No identifier normalization occurs.
```text target_digest = lowerhex(SHA256(RFC8785(target_identity))) gateway_request_key = "gw-" + lowerhex(SHA256(RFC8785( [profile_ref, send_id, attempt_id, target_digest, credential_scope]))) ```
RFC8785, not merely sorted keys, determines encoding. Secrets never enter keys or audit. Target, request bytes/digest, scope, attempt and key commit before network work. Exact replay retains all of them. A changed target/profile/credential or successor needs a new authorized attempt after reconciliation/proven stop. Credential revocation is `credential_scope_unavailable`, not permission to reuse the key with a new credential. Provisioning identity is never rewritten into delivery identity. `contracts/gateway-identity.md` owns this algorithm.
TABLE 5.1-2 — Replay and uncertainty
| Observation | Required action | Refused shortcut | |---|---|---| | Exact retained request | Return/replay its retained outcome | Another logical send | | Changed bytes under same identity | Conflict and authoritative readback | Overwrite retained request | | Lost allocation response | Lookup and verify original lineage | Speculative child | | Lost delivery response | Reconcile same attempt/runtime | Slot release or replacement | | Unavailable credential scope | Hold identity, authorize successor after uncertainty resolves | Substitute principal | | Retired native target | Explicit replacement with current policy | Recreate old identity |

## E.6 Fork, cross-profile transfer and restore
A same-profile fork records verified parent boundary, parent bond/session and explicit policy mode. D-038 defaults to `preserve_parent_snapshot`; authorized `current_policy` is the alternative. The modes are not a strictness order. Ordinary continuation and restart retain the live snapshot; no automatic resync occurs. Hermes retains ownership of native history, memory, learning and compaction.
Cross-profile or cross-host assignment is not native fork. It transfers only authorized context references. The destination allocates its own session with its own credentials and current policy. It inherits no sender authority or learned state. Unsupported native transfer fails before child creation; transcript synthesis is not a fallback.
Every archive restore or lost-session replacement resolves current permissions before activation under D-039, even with a complete archived policy. Archived source revision is history and may be null with a reason if absent; effective revision is separate and known. Restore never revives a revoked archived grant.

## E.7 Routing and roll-up example Task root 42 commits allocation A, then reconciled bond A/session A, then a NEW turn explicitly targeted to A. Root 57 independently commits allocation B/bond B/session B and targeted NEW. Repeated prompt text does not collapse their work identities. Subsequent REUSE turns retain each branch. Old-generation reports cannot close new attempts. Manager review produces one parent-thread report with child-report and artifact references, never a reconstructed transcript. Waiting preserves the logical obligation. Resume requires recorded approval/guard evidence and a successor attempt. Runtime terminal evidence separately controls reservation release. These are contract examples, not observed native executions. G-04 requires exact replay, changed target, credential rotation, cross-profile and lost-response traces; G-07 requires export→import→first-turn proof. **Full-size figure detail:** FIGURE 5.4-1 in §27; the detail sheets carry the drawing, explanation, steps and failure branches.
